source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed brake tests in a vehicle inspection report

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
- Identify the date and time of the inspection, as well as the vehicle identification number (VIN), make, model, and year of the vehicle being inspected.
3. Clearly note the specifics of the brake test performed. Document whether it was a road test, a pressure test, a hydraulic test, or a visual inspection. Describe the methodology and equipment used, such as brake meters or decelerometers.
4. Document the testing conditions. Note if the test was conducted on a flat, dry surface, or if weather conditions and road surface had potential impacts on the test results.
5. Record the specific brake components tested, including the front and rear brakes, parking brake, and any ABS (anti-lock braking system) components.
6. List the test measurements and the expected outcomes. Detail if and where measurements fell short; for instance, a brake force below minimum standards, uneven braking, excessive brake pedal travel, or other anomalies.
7. Provide an explanation
